# Make explicit automatic `OPTIONS` enablement effective

Flask allows automatic `OPTIONS` responses to be controlled globally and by
the `provide_automatic_options` attribute on a view function or `View` class.
The explicit view controls currently behave asymmetrically: they can disable
automatic handling, but an explicit `True` does not restore it when
`PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS` is disabled globally.

Correct route registration so explicit enablement is honored without changing
the default behavior.

- If a function view sets its `provide_automatic_options` attribute to true while the global default is false, its rule must include `OPTIONS` and use Flask's automatic response.
- If a class-based view sets its `provide_automatic_options` attribute to true while the global default is false, its rule must include `OPTIONS` and use Flask's automatic response.
- Explicit false values must continue to disable automatic handling, and a route that handles `OPTIONS` itself must continue to dispatch to that view.

Keep the existing `add_url_rule`, decorator, function-view, and class-based
view APIs intact. The relevant upstream coverage is in `tests/test_basic.py`
and `tests/test_views.py`; some assertions in those files describe behavior
that was corrected by the issue fix.

def test_options_work(app, client):
    @app.route("/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
    def index():
        return "Hello World"

    rv = client.open("/", method="OPTIONS")
    assert sorted(rv.allow) == ["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "POST"]
    assert rv.data == b""


def test_options_on_multiple_rules(app, client):

    @app.route("/", methods=["PUT"])

    rv = client.open("/", method="OPTIONS")

def test_provide_automatic_options_attr():
    app = flask.Flask(__name__)

    def index():
        return "Hello World!"

    index.provide_automatic_options = False
    app.route("/")(index)
    rv = app.test_client().open("/", method="OPTIONS")

def test_provide_automatic_options_kwarg(app, client):
    def index():
        return flask.request.method

    def more():
        return flask.request.method

    app.add_url_rule("/", view_func=index, provide_automatic_options=False)
    app.add_url_rule(
        "/more",
        view_func=more,
        methods=["GET", "POST"],
        provide_automatic_options=False,
    )
    assert client.get("/").data == b"GET"

    rv = client.post("/")

    assert sorted(rv.allow) == ["GET", "HEAD", "POST"]

def test_view_decorators(app, client):
    def add_x_parachute(f):
        def new_function(*args, **kwargs):
            resp = flask.make_response(f(*args, **kwargs))
            resp.headers["X-Parachute"] = "awesome"
            return resp

        return new_function

    class Index(flask.views.View):
        decorators = [add_x_parachute]

        def dispatch_request(self):
            return "Awesome"

    app.add_url_rule("/", view_func=Index.as_view("index"))
    rv = client.get("/")
    assert rv.headers["X-Parachute"] == "awesome"
    assert rv.data == b"Awesome"

    def add_url_rule(
        self,

        endpoint: str | None = None,
        view_func: ft.RouteCallable | None = None,
        provide_automatic_options: bool | None = None,
        **options: t.Any,
    ) -> None:
        if endpoint is None:
            endpoint = _endpoint_from_view_func(view_func)  # type: ignore
        options["endpoint"] = endpoint
        methods = options.pop("methods", None)

        # if the methods are not given and the view_func object knows its
        # methods we can use that instead.  If neither exists, we go with
        # a tuple of only ``GET`` as default.
        if methods is None:
            methods = getattr(view_func, "methods", None) or ("GET",)
        if isinstance(methods, str):
            raise TypeError(
                "Allowed methods must be a list of strings, for"
                ' example: @app.route(..., methods=["POST"])'

        methods = {item.upper() for item in methods}

        required_methods: set[str] = set(getattr(view_func, "required_methods", ()))

        # starting with Flask 0.8 the view_func object can disable and
        # force-enable the automatic options handling.

            provide_automatic_options = getattr(
                view_func, "provide_automatic_options", None

            if "OPTIONS" not in methods and self.config["PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS"]:
                provide_automatic_options = True
                required_methods.add("OPTIONS")

        methods |= required_methods

        rule_obj = self.url_rule_class(rule, methods=methods, **options)

                    f" endpoint function: {endpoint}"

        be used for every request.

        are forwarded to the view class ``__init__`` method.

            Added the ``init_every_request`` class attribute.

        view.view_class = cls  # type: ignore

def test_request_dispatching(app, client):
    @app.route("/")
    def index():
        return flask.request.method

    @app.route("/more", methods=["GET", "POST"])
    def more():
        return flask.request.method

    assert client.get("/").data == b"GET"
    rv = client.post("/")
    assert rv.status_code == 405
    assert sorted(rv.allow) == ["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"]
    rv = client.head("/")
    assert rv.status_code == 200
    assert not rv.data  # head truncates
    assert client.post("/more").data == b"POST"
    assert client.get("/more").data == b"GET"
    rv = client.delete("/more")
    assert rv.status_code == 405
    assert sorted(rv.allow) == ["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "POST"]

def test_url_mapping(app, client):
    random_uuid4 = "7eb41166-9ebf-4d26-b771-ea3f54f8b383"

    def index():
        return flask.request.method

    def more():
        return flask.request.method

    def options():
        return random_uuid4

    app.add_url_rule("/", "index", index)
    app.add_url_rule("/more", "more", more, methods=["GET", "POST"])

    # Issue 1288: Test that automatic options are not added

    app.add_url_rule("/options", "options", options, methods=["options"])

    assert client.get("/").data == b"GET"

    rv = client.head("/")
    assert rv.status_code == 200
    assert not rv.data  # head truncates
    assert client.post("/more").data == b"POST"
    assert client.get("/more").data == b"GET"
    rv = client.delete("/more")
    assert rv.status_code == 405
    assert sorted(rv.allow) == ["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "POST"]
    rv = client.open("/options", method="OPTIONS")
    assert rv.status_code == 200
    assert random_uuid4 in rv.data.decode("utf-8")
